chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Rashid said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: When Abd al-Muttalib dug Zamzam and reached

its bottom, there came out to him from one of the sides of the well a foul stench that alarmed him, but he refused to turn back. His son al-Harith came out from him. Then he dug until he went deep, and found at its bottom a spring flowing to him with the fragrance of musk. Then he dug, and had not dug more than a cubit when sleep overcame him. He saw a man of great stature, beautiful hair, handsome face, fine clothing, and pleasant fragrance, and he was saying: 'Dig and you will gain! Strive and you will be safe! Do not hoard it for the distribution. The swords are for others, and the well is for you!'

The well is for you. You are the greatest of the Arabs in honor, and from you will emerge its Prophet and its Guardian, and the noble descendants — the wise, the scholars, the perspicacious. And the swords are for them. But they are not today from you nor for you; rather in the second generation from you. By them God will illuminate the earth, bring out the devils from its corners, humiliate them in their might, destroy them after their strength, humiliate the idols, and kill their worshippers wherever they may be. Then after him there will remain a descendant from your descendants — he will be his brother and his vizier, lesser than him in age, able against the idols, not

disobeying him in a single letter, concealing nothing from him, and consulting him in every matter that befalls him.' Abd al-Muttalib was exhausted from this. He found thirteen swords leaning to his side. He took them and intended to spread the news, but said: 'How can I, when I have not yet reached the water?' Then he dug, and had not dug a palm's width when the horn of the gazelle appeared to him along with its head. He extracted it, and inscribed on it was: 'There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God; Ali is the Guardian of God;

Ali is the Guardian of God; so-and-so is the Caliph of God.' I asked him and said: 'So-and-so — when will he be, before him or after him?' He said: 'He has not yet come, nor has any of his signs appeared.' Abd al-Muttalib came out, having extracted the water. As he was ascending, there was a black creature with a long tail rushing ahead of him to the top. He struck it and cut off most of its tail, then sought it but it escaped. And so-and-so shall kill it, God willing. Abd al-Muttalib considered invalidating the dream he had seen in the well and placing the swords as coverings of the Kaaba. But God brought sleep upon him while he was in the Hijr of the Kaaba, and he saw that same man

saying: 'O Shayba al-Hamd! Praise your Lord, for He will make you the tongue of the earth, and the Quraysh will follow you out of fear, awe, and desire. Place the swords in their places.' Abd al-Muttalib woke up and replied to him that he comes to me in sleep; if he is from my Lord, then he is more beloved to me; and if he is from a devil, then I think it has had its tail cut off. But he neither saw anything nor heard any speech. Then when night came, he came to him in his dream with a group of men and children, who said to him: 'We are the followers of your children, and we are from the dwellers of the sixth heaven. The swords are not for you. Marry among the Makhzum to gain strength, and then trade among the tribes of the Arabs. If you have no wealth, then you have noble lineage. Hand over these thirteen

swords to the children of the Makhzumi woman, and no more than this will be revealed to you. And one sword from them is for you — it will fall from your hand and you will find no trace of it, except that such-and-such a mountain will conceal it, and it will be among the signs of the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad (may God bless him and them).' Abd al-Muttalib awoke and set out with the swords on his neck. He came to an area around Mecca and lost one sword — the finest among them with him — it will appear from there. He then entered for 'Umra and circumambulated with them on his neck along with the two gazelle horns, twenty-one circumambulations, while the Quraysh watched him, and he was saying: 'O God! Confirm Your promise, establish my word, spread my mention, and strengthen my arm.' This was his constant speech; and after his dream in the well

he did not circumambulate the House with a single verse of poetry until he died. But he did recite a rajaz poem to his children on the day he intended to sacrifice Abdullah. He handed over all the swords to the children of the Makhzumi woman — to al-Zubayr, to Abu Talib, and to Abdullah. Four swords went to Abu Talib: a sword for Abu Talib, a sword for Ali, a sword for Ja'far, and a sword for Talib. Al-Zubayr received two swords, and Abdullah received two swords. Then they reverted, and the remaining four went to Ali — two from Fatima and two from her children. The sword of Ja'far was lost on the day he was killed, and it is not known in whose hands it fell until this hour. And we say: no sword from our swords falls into the hands of others — except for a man who aids

with it alongside us — but it turns to coal. He said: Among them is one in a certain location that comes out like a snake emerges, so that a cubit of it and what resembles it appears, and the earth shines for it time and again, then it disappears. And when night comes, it does the same. This will be its habit until its master comes. And if I wished to name its place I would name it, but I fear for you that if I name it, you would disclose its name, and it would be attributed to other than what it truly is.

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim — the kunya of Imam Musa al-Kazim (as), the 7th Imam
key_terms.الْأَسْيَاف: The swords — thirteen sacred swords found at Zamzam with prophetic and eschatological significance
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im — the Rising One, referring to the awaited 12th Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.زَمْزَم: Zamzam — the sacred well of Mecca, associated with Hagar and Ishmael, discovered/rediscovered by Abd al-Muttalib
key_terms.شَيْبَةَ الْحَمْد: Shayba al-Hamd — an honorific of Abd al-Muttalib meaning 'the gray-haired one worthy of praise'

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim narrate about Abd al-Muttalib digging Zamzam and the prophetic swords?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (as), the seventh Imam, narrates to his companion al-Hasan ibn Rashid a detailed account of Abd al-Muttalib's discovery of the Zamzam well, including prophetic visions he received during sleep foretelling the emergence of the Prophet Muhammad (saww) and Imam Ali (as) from his lineage, as well as the miraculous swords found at Zamzam that carry eschatological significance tied to the Qa'im (the awaited Imam). The hadith reveals the pre-Islamic divine preparation for the prophetic mission, demonstrates Abd al-Muttalib's noble and persevering character, and establishes a direct link between the physical discovery of Zamzam and the spiritual destiny of the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of the sword lost at Ja'far ibn Abi Talib's martyrdom and the hidden sword awaiting the Qa'im connects this pre-Islamic narrative to Shia eschatological belief.
